builtinCommands.$comment: Built-in Cargo commands (`commands::builtin_exec`). An alias with one of these names is discarded at startup with `user-defined alias <name> is ignored, because it is shadowed by a built-in command`. The built-in aliases `b`, `c`, `d`, `t`, `r` and `rm` are deliberately absent: a user alias takes precedence over those. Referenced from `propertyNames` under `not`.

cargoInvocationToken.$comment: A first token that names the `cargo` binary (bare, `.exe`-suffixed or path-qualified) or a `cargo-<name>` subcommand binary. `cargofmt` and other tokens that merely begin with the letters `cargo` are not matched, since those are legitimate alias or subcommand names.

toolchainOrOptionToken.$comment: A first token starting with `-` (parsed as an unexpected argument, since the subcommand must come first) or `+` (a rustup toolchain directive that Cargo itself cannot resolve).

title: [alias]
description:
Cargo command aliases. Each key is a subcommand name; the value is the command to run, either a single string (split on whitespace) or an array of arguments. Aliases are recursive and may not redefine existing built-in Cargo commands. Per-alias values can also be set via the `CARGO_ALIAS_<name>` environment variable.

The value continues the `cargo` command line, so it must not repeat `cargo` itself: write `run --release`, not `cargo run --release`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#alias)

additionalProperties.title: alias expansion
additionalProperties.description:
Command the alias expands to, written as it appears after `cargo`. The first token is the subcommand and may be a built-in command, another alias, or an external `cargo-<name>` subcommand.

The leading `cargo` is implied: write `run --release`, not `cargo run --release`.

oneOf.title: command string
oneOf.description: Subcommand and arguments, split on whitespace.

allOf.$comment: The expansion is appended to `cargo`, so a leading `cargo` produces `cargo cargo ...` and fails with a `no such command` error. A leading `cargo-<name>` fails the same way, because Cargo resolves external subcommands by searching for `cargo-cargo-<name>`.

The expansion must start with a subcommand. A leading option fails with `unexpected argument`, and a leading `+toolchain` fails with `no such command`, since rustup, not Cargo, resolves toolchain directives.

oneOf.title: argument list
oneOf.description: Subcommand followed by arguments, passed through verbatim. Use this form to preserve arguments containing spaces.

prefixItems.description: Subcommand the alias expands to: a single token, with no embedded whitespace.

allOf.$comment: The expansion is appended to `cargo`, so a leading `cargo` produces `cargo cargo ...` and fails with a `no such command` error. A leading `cargo-<name>` fails the same way, because Cargo resolves external subcommands by searching for `cargo-cargo-<name>`.

The expansion must start with a subcommand. A leading option fails with `unexpected argument`, and a leading `+toolchain` fails with `no such command`, since rustup, not Cargo, resolves toolchain directives.

propertyNames.description: Cargo subcommand name: a non-empty token with no whitespace. `.` is the configuration path separator and cannot appear in an addressable alias name, and a leading `-` or `+` can never be typed as a subcommand. Names of built-in Cargo commands are rejected because Cargo ignores aliases that shadow them.

docs.main:
Defines [Cargo command aliases](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#alias).

Each key is the subcommand name and the value is what `cargo <key>` expands to. Use a string (split on whitespace) or an array (preserves whitespace inside arguments).

**Built-in aliases** (may be overridden): `b` → `build`, `c` → `check`, `d` → `doc`, `t` → `test`, `r` → `run`, `rm` → `remove`.

Aliases are recursive — one alias may invoke another. Aliases may **not** redefine existing built-in Cargo commands.

The value continues the command line after `cargo`, so it must not start with `cargo` or `cargo-<name>`, with an option, or with a `+toolchain` directive.

Each alias may also be set via the `CARGO_ALIAS_<name>` environment variable.
